# Findings

*The brainstorm for CR-2609-823a — a to-do list. Rewritten in full after every answer, so an
interrupted conversation still leaves a complete document.*

**Is this one change?** Yes. One to-do list and one screen: adding a task, ticking it done,
editing it and deleting it all live in one place. The one part that could have been a change of
its own was removing the guestbook, and the user chose to keep it (Q-1).

## What was settled

Already settled by the request or by the specification, and therefore not asked:

- **Anybody can add a task.** "chce by kazdy mogl dodac nowe zadanie" (`request.md`, line 5) —
  it agrees with the standing non-goal: no accounts, sessions or roles
  (`spec/invariants.md` § Deliberate non-goals).
- **One simple view:** one field to add a task, and the list of the tasks added below it
  (`request.md`, line 5).
- **Each task in the list has a way to mark it done** (`request.md`, line 5).
- **The list is kept by the application, not by the browser.** Everybody sees the same list;
  "the browser stores nothing" (`spec/design/ui/system-states.md`, lines 156-157).

Round 1 — asked, answered 2026-09-24:

- **Q-1 — Beside the guestbook, or replacing it?** → **Beside it; the guestbook stays.**
  - The application gets a second screen, and people need a way to switch between the two.
    The frame promises exactly that: a second screen "must add navigation here"
    (`spec/design/ui/system-states.md` § One column).
  - Copy that says the application has one screen stops being true: the 404 sentence "There
    is one screen in this application: the guestbook." (`system-states.md`, line 134).
  - Removing the guestbook is **not** part of this change.
- **Q-2 — Can a done task be switched back to not done?** → **Yes, it can be switched back.**
  - Done is a two-way switch: ticking marks the task done, and ticking again marks it not done.
    This settles the reading of "odznaczenia" in the request as a toggle.
- **Q-3 — Which of "ew usuniecie lub edycja" belong in this change?** → **Both delete and
  edit.**
  - "ew." is settled as *and also*, not as *maybe later*. Every task can have its text changed
    and can be removed.
- **Q-4 — What happens to a task once it is marked done?** → **It stays in its place, shown as
  done.**
  - Ticking never moves a task. Done tasks are shown differently from open ones (for example
    ticked or crossed out), and the list order does not depend on done or not done.

Round 2 — asked, answered 2026-09-24:

- **Q-5 — With two screens, which one opens at the main address?** → **The guestbook, as
  today.**
  - `/` keeps going to the guestbook (`frontend/src/router.tsx:29`), and the smoke test that
    pins it (`e2e/ui/test_smoke.py::test_the_root_redirects_to_the_one_screen`) keeps its
    meaning. Only its name, "the one screen", stops being true.
  - The to-do list gets an address of its own and is reached through the navigation.
- **Q-6 — In what order are the tasks listed?** → **Newest at the top.**
  - A task just added appears first, right under the field. Together with Q-4, the order is
    by when a task was added, and ticking done never changes it.
  - Two tasks added at the same instant still need a fixed order, which the guestbook gets
    from a tie-break (`spec/contexts/guestbook.md` § `BR-04`). The requirements author picks
    that up.
- **Q-7 — Which language does the to-do screen use?** → **English, like the rest.**
  - Copy follows `spec/design/conventions.md` § Language. No rule is lifted. The request was
    written in Polish; the screen is not.
- **Q-8 — Does a fresh copy of the app start with example tasks?** → **Yes, a few example
  tasks.**
  - The seed half of the corpus (`golden-set/seed/`) gets example tasks, and the seeder has to
    post them. Today it knows `/guestbook-entries` alone and refuses a guest book that already
    has entries (`scripts/seed_golden_set.py:70`; `spec/design/architecture.md` § What a new
    environment starts with).
  - **This reaches `scripts/`.** `impact.md` recorded `tooling_touched` as absent on exactly
    this condition: "reached only if the requirements give the list seed data" (§ What I
    could not determine; § Tier signals). The condition is now met, so the recorded
    measurement is out of date. See § Open.

## What the user said and the system does differently

- *Nothing so far.* Every answer stays inside what the specification allows. Q-1 keeps the
  guestbook, which `spec/contexts/guestbook.md` (lines 17-19) calls the example the first real
  feature replaces. That is a choice the specification leaves open, not a conflict with it.

## Rules no document carried

- **A task's "done" can be undone** (Q-2). Today no stored thing in this system has a state:
  a guestbook entry "either exists or it does not" (`spec/contexts/guestbook.md` § `P-01`).
  The to-do list brings in the first stored state, and it is reversible.
- **Ticking done never moves a task** (Q-4, Q-6). The list has one order, newest first, and
  done or not done plays no part in it.

## Deliberately out of scope

- **Removing or changing the guestbook** — the user chose to keep it (Q-1).
- **A Polish screen** — the screen is English, like the rest (Q-7).

## Open

- **The read-back is next.** Assumptions for the smaller details are put to the user in one
  go, and they can object to any of them.
- **For the orchestrator: the recorded tier signals are out of date.** Q-8 lights
  `tooling_touched`, which `impact.md` recorded as absent on the condition Q-8 has now met.
  The tier does not move (`new_context` alone gives p3). The record should say what the change
  reaches before the design stage reads it.

When an answer in the `cr-brainstorm` pre-step lights, or rules out, a tier signal that `cr-impact` measured before the brainstorm, the recorded signals are re-measured before the requirements stage closes. Today no step does it; the orchestrator has to notice and improvise.

## 2. The coupling surface

- The composition of the `requirements` stage: `cr-impact` goes out in wave 1 and measures the signals, then the `cr-brainstorm` pre-step reads `impact.md`, then waves 2 and 3.
- The state verb `sdd-engine change_state set-signals`, which only `cr-impact` (and `cr-request`) call.
- The steps `.specconf/process.json` § `conditional` selects from those signals.

## 4. Expected, and by which authority

Nothing documents what happens when the brainstorm moves a signal, and that is the finding.

- It also says the signals are recorded "both halves, the lit one and the dark one, because 'not lit' is a measurement and silence is not", and that "the same signals that set the tier also select the conditional steps in every later stage — there is no second decision" (`skills/cr-impact/SKILL.md` § FAN-OUT CONTRACT).

The brainstorm exists to settle what `impact.md` could not determine. So it is, by design, the step most likely to turn an "absent, unless the user asks for X" into "present". Yet the only verb that records the measurement belongs to a step that has already run (`cr-impact`; the grep above). `skills/sdd/references/tiers-and-signals.md` names no re-measurement.

## 5. How it was discovered

- **Repository and branch:** jarekwasowskiscalo/forge-test2-react, branch `sdd/CR-2609-823a-todo-list-add-tasks-and-mark-them-done`
- **Change record:** CR-2609-823a ("Todo list - add tasks and mark them done"). No pull request yet.
- **Where in the process:** stage `requirements`, right after the `cr-brainstorm` pre-step (main conversation) and before wave 2 (`cr-requirements`). The brainstorm flagged it for the orchestrator in `brainstorm.md` § Open.
- **Queue entry:** banked as PROC-4

## 6. Reproduction

1. Open a change whose `impact.md` records a path signal as absent on a stated condition, which the brainstorm then settles. Here: `tooling_touched`, absent "only if the requirements give the list seed data".
2. Run the `cr-brainstorm` pre-step and answer so the condition is met (Q-8: example tasks on a fresh environment, which reaches `scripts/seed_golden_set.py`).
3. `sdd-engine loop next` offers wave 2 with the COMPOSITION computed from the old record. No row asks for a re-measurement, and `cr-brainstorm`'s write set is `brainstorm.md` alone, so it cannot record one.

## 7. Root cause, so far

**CONFIRMED by reading:**
- The requirements stage measures in wave 1, before its pre-step (the injected contract; the orchestrator's pipeline table in `skills/sdd/SKILL.md`).
- `set-signals` is called only by `cr-impact` and `cr-request` (the grep above).
- `cr-brainstorm` may write `brainstorm.md` and nothing else (its preflight: "YOU MAY WRITE — nothing outside this list: {change_dir}"; its iron rule 6).

**Not investigated:** whether any later gate compares the recorded path signals against the paths the final diff reaches. If one does, it would catch this at delivery, after the design and implement compositions had already been chosen from the stale record.

## 8. Why this level cannot fix it alone

The stage's composition, the order of its members and the verbs that record the signals are the engine's. An instance cannot add a step to the requirements stage or give the brainstorm a state verb.

- **Considered at this level, and done as the workaround:** the orchestrator re-runs `set-signals` by hand. It works only when somebody notices. Here it was noticed because `impact.md` happened to write the condition down, and `brainstorm.md` happened to flag it.
- **Not the template's:** the template carries no part of the stage composition beyond the seeded `process.json`.
- **Not this repository's own application or specification.**

## 9. Proposed resolution

**Proposed:** make the re-measurement a named move at the one point where it can matter, between the brainstorm and wave 2. For example:
- `cr-brainstorm`'s closing block (or a section of `brainstorm.md`) carries a `SIGNALS:` line naming every signal an answer lit or ruled out, with the answer that did it.
- `sdd-engine loop next` then renders the `set-signals` call, or refuses to dispatch wave 2 while such a line is unrecorded.

The measurement stays in the record, re-taken rather than overwritten, and the action log shows which answer moved it.

**Rejected, and why:**
- (a) Run `cr-impact` after the brainstorm. The brainstorm needs `impact.md` to ask good questions; its iron rule 0 is "Read `impact.md` in full before the first question".
- (b) Have `cr-requirements` re-measure from `requirements.md`. It works, but it moves the measurement to a worker whose skill is about EARS sentences, and it runs after the brainstorm's answers could already have shaped wave 2's composition.
- (c) Leave it to the orchestrator's attention. That is what happened here.

## 10. Blast radius

- **Which stacks does this touch?** Every stack. The requirements stage and its pre-step are the engine's.
- **Does the other template survive the change unmodified?** Yes. No stack-side file needs to move.
- **Is it backwards compatible with profiles already committed?** Yes. `set-signals` already replaces the measurement, so re-taking it needs no new state shape.
- **Does `schema_version` move?** Not by this proposal.
- **Does any archived change record stop being readable?** No.
- **Which existing tests must change?** The orchestrator's table tests, if a row or a refusal is added. Not investigated.

## 11. Acceptance criteria

1. In a fixture change whose brainstorm answer meets a condition `impact.md` stated for an absent signal, `sdd-engine loop next` after the pre-step either renders the `set-signals` call naming that signal, or refuses to dispatch wave 2 until it is recorded.
2. After it, `sdd-engine change_state show --cr <CR> --field signals` lists the signal as present, and the action log names the brainstorm answer that moved it.
3. The design stage's `COMPOSITION` line is computed from the re-taken measurement.

**Proved by:** a new test beside `skills/_shared/sdd/test_sdd_state_verbs.py` and the orchestrator's table tests; the implementer names it.

## 12. What this repository does meanwhile

- [ ] **Blocked**
- [x] **Working around it** — and the workaround is at: the hand-run `set-signals` on CR-2609-823a (action log of that change record), explained in `spec/changes/CR-2609-823a-todo-list-add-tasks-and-mark-them-done/brainstorm.md` § Open.
- [ ] **Nothing** — it was noticed, not hit

**Must the workaround be reverted when this lands?** No. The record now says what the change reaches; there is nothing to undo.

## 13. Not this

- Not a change to the signal definitions (that is #296, filed from the same change).
- Not a change to `cr-impact` running first.
- Here the tier did not move (`new_context` gives p3 either way) and no conditional step changed. The finding is the missing step, not a wrong tier on this change.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Post-step verification for cr-scenarios: does every scenario prove a requirement?

Two of this skill's own rules were stated five times each in its SKILL.md and
checked by nothing: every scenario carries the identifier of the requirement it
proves, and a scenario never names a URL, an HTTP verb or a status code. A rule
repeated five times in prose and zero times in code is a rule that survives
exactly as long as the model's attention does.

The third check is the one the audit paid for. Session `9a60261d` spent a whole
subagent -- 45 turns, 4.5M tokens -- on a task recorded as "Fix scenarios bullet
list", a formatting defect that had survived two coherence rounds. Structure is
cheap to check and expensive to review.

Usage:
    sdd-skill cr-scenarios resources/cr_scenarios_verify.py --cr CR-2608-9373

Output: one JSON object on stdout.
Exit codes: 0 = all pass, 1 = any fail. Warnings never change the code.
"""

import argparse
import json
import pathlib
import re
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "_shared"))

from sdd import change_state, verify_lib

#: Gherkin is business language. A scenario that names a route or a status code has
#: encoded the design into the artefact a non-programmer is supposed to read.
_FORBIDDEN = (
    (re.compile(r"\b(GET|POST|PUT|PATCH|DELETE)\b"), "an HTTP verb"),
    (re.compile(r"\b[45]\d{2}\b"), "a status code"),
    (re.compile(r"/api/"), "a URL path"),
)

_SCENARIO = re.compile(r"^\s*Scenario(?: Outline)?:", re.MULTILINE)


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="cr-scenarios post-step verification")
    parser.add_argument("--cr", required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    result = verify_lib.Result("cr-scenarios")
    try:
        change_dir = change_state.change_dir(args.cr)
    except change_state.StateError as error:
        print(json.dumps({"ok": False, "skill": "cr-scenarios", "errors": [str(error)]}))
        return 1

    scenarios = change_dir / "scenarios.md"
    requirements = change_dir / "requirements.md"
    result.files.append(verify_lib.check_file(scenarios))

    if not result.check("output_exists", scenarios.is_file(), f"missing: {scenarios}"):
        print(json.dumps(result.payload(), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
        return 1

    text = scenarios.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    # 1. There are scenarios at all.
    count = len(_SCENARIO.findall(text))
    result.check("scenario_count", count > 0, "no `Scenario:` block found", value=count)

    # 2. Every declared requirement is proved by at least one scenario, and every
    #    tag resolves. A typo in an identifier looks exactly like coverage.
    tags = set(verify_lib.parse_req_tags(text))
    declared = (
        {req.rid for req in verify_lib.parse_requirements(requirements.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))}
        if requirements.is_file()
        else set()
    )
    qualified = {tag.split("/", 1)[1] for tag in tags}
    unresolved = sorted(rid for rid in qualified if declared and rid not in declared)
    result.check(
        "tags_resolve",
        not unresolved,
        f"scenario tags name requirements that do not exist: {', '.join(unresolved)}",
        tags=sorted(tags),
    )
    uncovered = sorted(declared - qualified)
    result.check(
        "every_requirement_covered",
        not uncovered,
        f"no scenario proves: {', '.join(uncovered)}",
    )

    # 3. Every scenario is tagged. An untagged one proves nothing traceable.
    if count and not tags:
        result.check("scenarios_tagged", False, "no `@req:CR-*/R-n` tag anywhere in the document")

    # 4. Business language only -- in the steps, not in the prose explaining them.
    steps = verify_lib.gherkin_steps(text)
    for pattern, what in _FORBIDDEN:
        offending = next((line for line in steps if pattern.search(line)), None)
        result.check(
            f"no_{what.replace(' ', '_')}_in_steps",
            offending is None,
            f"a scenario step names {what}: {offending.strip()!r}. Gherkin here is the "
            "artefact a non-programmer reads."
            if offending
            else "",
        )

    # 5. Structure, the defect that cost a subagent. Every Gherkin step line sits
    #    under a Scenario, and a bullet list is not a step.
    stray = [
        line
        for line in text.splitlines()
        if re.match(r"^\s*[-*]\s+(Given|When|Then|And|But)\b", line)
    ]
    result.check(
        "steps_are_not_bullets",
        not stray,
        f"{len(stray)} Gherkin step(s) written as markdown bullets, e.g. {stray[0].strip()!r}"
        if stray

## 1. What must become true

`cr_scenarios_verify.py`'s `every_requirement_covered` check does not demand a scenario for a requirement that carries `**Verified-by:** manual — <reason>`. The scenario author is never forced to tag seeds `@req <R-n>` for a requirement no automated suite may cite.

## 2. The coupling surface

- The post-step verifier of a SKILL: `skills/cr-scenarios/resources/cr_scenarios_verify.py`.
- The traceability surface it feeds: the `@req` tags that `build-tests-e2e` turns into Gherkin tags.

## 3. Observed

```text
The cr-scenarios worker's closing block, PROCESS_FAULT, verbatim:
cr_scenarios_verify.py's every_requirement_covered does not exempt a `**Verified-by:** manual`
requirement, so R-11 had to get seeds tagged @req R-11 that the black box must not bind (it starts
with --no-seed). This invites build-tests-e2e to put a citation beside the manual marker.

plugin 0.1.126, skills/cr-scenarios/resources/cr_scenarios_verify.py:69-89:
    tags = set(verify_lib.parse_req_tags(text))
    declared = (
        {req.rid for req in verify_lib.parse_requirements(requirements.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))}
        if requirements.is_file()
        else set()
    )
    qualified = {tag.split("/", 1)[1] for tag in tags}
    ...
    uncovered = sorted(declared - qualified)
    result.check(
        "every_requirement_covered",
        not uncovered,
        f"no scenario proves: {', '.join(uncovered)}",
    )

The requirement it forced seeds for (CR-2609-823a requirements.md, R-11):
**Verified-by:** manual — the seeder is proved by `tests/tooling/` and the seed corpus by
`tests/fitness/`, neither of which carries a requirement citation by rule (`spec/design/testing.md`
§ The UI smoke is not a traceability surface), and the black box starts the application with
`--no-seed`; a person opens a freshly created environment and counts the example tasks.

The engine already parses the marker: skills/_shared/sdd/verify_lib.py:180
MANUAL: Final = re.compile(r"\*\*Verified-by:\*\*\s*manual\s*[-—]+\s*(?P<reason>.+)")
```

**Plugin version:** 0.1.126. Read from the skill base directory (`~/.claude/plugins/cache/scalo/forge/0.1.126/`) and from `sdd-engine loop sent`, which printed `"toolchain": {"chain": "forge 0.1.126"}`.

**Stack:** `fastapi-react-postgres`

**Level:** instance

**Repository, and its commit:** jarekwasowskiscalo/forge-test2-react@68c647394b35c280b17fafeb0f8f4c49cba7fe09

**Its template:** Scalo-Sales-Engineering-Consulting/forge_template_python_react

## 4. Expected, and by which authority

Article III of the constitution, as the template carries it (`spec/constitution.md` § Article III): *"Where a requirement genuinely cannot be tested automatically, it says so about itself in its own text (`**Verified-by:** manual — <reason>`). The exception is then counted and printed."*

The engine's own gate treats the marker as the exit. `spec_gates.py:276`: *"`**Verified-by:** manual -- <reason>` in the artefact IS the exit"*.

The scenario verifier is the one place that still demands an automated-style proof for it: a seed tagged `@req`, which the next author (`build-tests-e2e`) is told to turn into a bound Gherkin tag.

## 5. How it was discovered

- **Repository and branch:** jarekwasowskiscalo/forge-test2-react, branch `sdd/CR-2609-823a-todo-list-add-tasks-and-mark-them-done`
- **Change record:** CR-2609-823a ("Todo list - add tasks and mark them done"). No pull request yet.
- **Where in the process:** stage `requirements`, wave 3, skill `cr-scenarios` (a dispatched worker on opus). R-11, the example tasks a new environment starts with, is `**Verified-by:** manual`.
- **Queue entry:** banked as PROC-6

## 6. Reproduction

1. Write a `requirements.md` in which one requirement carries `**Verified-by:** manual — <reason>`.
2. Write a `scenarios.md` that seeds every other requirement and none for that one.
3. `sdd-skill cr-scenarios resources/cr_scenarios_verify.py --cr <CR>` fails `every_requirement_covered` with "no scenario proves: R-n".

## 7. Root cause, so far

**CONFIRMED (read at the cited lines):** `declared` is every requirement id `parse_requirements` returns. Nothing subtracts the ones `verify_lib.MANUAL` matches before `declared - qualified`.

**HYPOTHESIS, not investigated:** whether `traceability` or `build-tests-e2e`'s own verify then refuses a requirement that is both marked manual and cited by a bound scenario. The worker's concern is that the forced seed invites exactly that citation.

## 8. Why this level cannot fix it alone

The verifier ships inside the plugin's `cr-scenarios` skill and runs from the plugin cache. An instance cannot change it.

- **Considered at this level:** dropping `**Verified-by:** manual` from R-11 so the verifier and the gate agree. Rejected: R-11 genuinely cannot be proved by a citing suite on this stack (the black box runs `--no-seed`, and `tests/tooling/` and `tests/fitness/` cite no requirement by rule), so removing the marker would make the requirement lie.
- **Not the template's.**

## 9. Proposed resolution

**Proposed:** subtract the manual requirements before the coverage check, the way the gate already treats them:

```python
manual = {req.rid for req in parsed if req.manual}   # or verify_lib.MANUAL over each block
uncovered = sorted(declared - manual - qualified)
```

Optionally keep a warning, never a failure, naming the manual requirements, so the count stays printed as Article III asks. Separately, decide whether a seed tagged for a manual requirement should itself be refused, so a citation never sits beside the marker.

**Rejected, and why:**
- (a) Require a seed but tag it differently (e.g. `@manual`). A second tag grammar for one exception, which every downstream reader then has to learn.
- (b) Leave it and rely on `build-tests-e2e` not binding the seed. That is the invitation this issue is about.

## 10. Blast radius

- **Which stacks does this touch?** Every stack. The verifier is the engine's.
- **Does the other template survive the change unmodified?** Yes.
- **Is it backwards compatible with profiles already committed?** Yes.
- **Does `schema_version` move?** No.
- **Does any archived change record stop being readable?** No.
- **Which existing tests must change?** The cr-scenarios verifier's tests, if any pin the current behaviour; a new case for a manual requirement.

## 11. Acceptance criteria

1. A `requirements.md` with R-1 (automated) and R-2 (`**Verified-by:** manual — <reason>`), plus a `scenarios.md` seeding R-1 only: `cr_scenarios_verify.py --cr <CR>` exits 0, and `every_requirement_covered` passes.
2. The same with R-1 unseeded still fails, naming R-1 and not R-2.

**Proved by:** a new test beside the cr-scenarios verifier's tests.

## 12. What this repository does meanwhile

- [ ] **Blocked**
- [x] **Working around it** — and the workaround is at: `spec/changes/CR-2609-823a-todo-list-add-tasks-and-mark-them-done/scenarios.md`, the seeds tagged `@req` R-11, which the worker notes the black box must not bind.
- [ ] **Nothing** — it was noticed, not hit

**Must the workaround be reverted when this lands?** Yes, in spirit. `build-tests-e2e` must not bind the R-11 seeds in this change; once the fix lands, a later change need not write them.

## 13. Not this

- Not a change to Article III or to the `traceability` gate.
- Not a change to what a manual requirement owes in `uat.md`.

*ONE file for the whole change, one section per pass.*

## Pass 1 — the `requirements` stage

First pass of the stage (a full hunt). There are no recorded resolutions yet, so Phase 1b had
nothing to verify. Artefacts read: `brainstorm.md`, `impact.md`, `requirements.md` (with Edge
cases and Impact analysis), `scenarios.md` (with Test data), and the three `ASSUMPTIONS` blocks
from the preflight. The ranked documents read above them: `spec/constitution.md`,
`spec/invariants.md`, `spec/glossary.md`, `contracts/README.md`.

The answers to `Q-10`, `Q-11` and `Q-12` were read from the record, because no Markdown
document carries them. Command:
`sdd-engine change_state show --cr CR-2609-823a --field open_questions`. Output: `Q-10` →
`A` "Yes, each list is filled on its own" (answered 2026-09-24T12:14:04Z); `Q-11` → `A` "Refuse
it, with its own message" (12:14:05Z); `Q-12` → `A` "Yes, at least one is done" (12:14:05Z).

Pairs compared: brainstorm ↔ requirements (every `Q-1`…`Q-9` answer and all eight read-back
assumptions); requirements § Requirements ↔ scenarios (all 53 seeds, one by one); requirements
§ Requirements ↔ § Edge cases and § Non-Goals; requirements ↔ impact; scenarios § Test data ↔
the corpus rules and the trim set; every artefact ↔ the glossary; every artefact ↔
`spec/invariants.md` and `contracts/invariants/guestbook.md`; each author's assumptions ↔ what
its neighbour wrote.

### COH-requirements-1 — Is a line break inside a task's text refused, or still an open question?

- **kind:** gap
- **severity:** major
- **decision_mode:** HITL

content.content:
198	### COH-requirements-4 — Which characters count as "a line break" inside a task?
199	
200	- **kind:** quality
201	- **severity:** major
202	- **decision_mode:** HITL
203	- **auto_basis:**
204	- **ambiguity_source:** spec/changes/CR-2609-823a-todo-list-add-tasks-and-mark-them-done/requirements.md § R-2
205	- **artifacts:** requirements.md, scenarios.md
206	
207	**What each says.** `requirements.md` § R-2 clause 4 uses "a line break" without naming its
208	characters, and clause 5 demands that the screen accept "exactly the texts the service accepts".
209	`scenarios.md` uses U+000A alone. Its § Bounds the requirements did not give, item 1, reports that
210	U+000D, U+0085, U+2028, U+2029, U+000B and U+000C are unstated. It also notes that the guestbook
211	keeps a next line inside a signature (`text-measurement.json` case `next_line_inside_is_kept`,
212	present: checked by loading the file).
213	
214	**Why they cannot both be true.** Clause 5 cannot hold if the two sides each take their own
215	language's default, and the defaults disagree. Command: `python3 -c` over
216	`str.splitlines()`, then `node -e` over `/^.*$/`. Output: `python splitlines breaks on: ['LF',
217	'VT', 'FF', 'CR', 'NEL', 'LS', 'PS']` against `js ... breaks on: [ 'LF', 'CR', 'LS', 'PS' ]`. A
218	task carrying VT, FF or NEL between two words would be refused by the service and let through by
219	the screen. That is the `D-04` class of defect `requirements.md` § Edge cases lists as having
220	happened, and the reason `spec/contexts/guestbook.md` § `BR-01` writes its trim set down ("the
221	two languages this system is built in disagree about six of them").
222	
223	**What settles it.** Nothing. Which texts a person may store is a product rule.
224	
225	**Resolution.** Ask one closed question. (A, recommended) A line break is any of U+000A, U+000B,
226	U+000C, U+000D, U+0085, U+2028, U+2029: one written set that both sides read and no language
227	default, so a pasted text is refused identically everywhere. (B) U+000A and U+000D only: the
228	others stay content, as in a guestbook signature, and the written set is those two. Then add the
229	chosen set to the new `R-2` clause 6 (COH-requirements-1) and to § Bounds as "| Line break inside
230	a task | refused; the set is … | `Q-11`, this decision |".
231	
232	**What was ambiguous.** `requirements.md` § R-2 clause 4 introduced "line break" as a term.
233	`Q-11`'s wording ("a line break inside a task's text") inherited it, and neither gave the set.
234	
235	**What was not found.** No artefact asserts which refusal wins when a text is both over 200 and
236	multi-line. Neither says it, so nothing contradicts. It is not raised here.
237	
238	### COH-requirements-5 — Does the standing non-goal on authentication and retention cover tasks?
239	
240	- **kind:** gap
241	- **severity:** minor
242	- **decision_mode:** HITL
243	- **auto_basis:**
244	- **ambiguity_source:** spec/invariants.md § Deliberate non-goals
245	- **artifacts:** requirements.md, spec/invariants.md
246	
247	**What each says.** `requirements.md` § Non-Goals: "This is the standing non-goal
248	(`spec/invariants.md` § Deliberate non-goals): anybody adds, marks, edits and deletes any task",
249	and "a task lives until somebody deletes it". `spec/invariants.md` § Deliberate non-goals, lines
250	123-125: "anybody may add, amend and delete any entry". Line 162: "An entry lives until somebody
251	deletes it."
252	
253	**Why they cannot both be true.** `requirements.md` cites the standing non-goal as covering tasks,
254	and the cited text covers entries only. `requirements.md` itself says so, "By intent yes, by
255	wording no" (Self-check 23, and § Impact analysis). It reports this for the convergence round,

### COH-requirements-4 — Which characters count as "a line break" inside a task?

- **kind:** quality
- **severity:** major
- **decision_mode:** HITL
- **auto_basis:**
- **ambiguity_source:** spec/changes/CR-2609-823a-todo-list-add-tasks-and-mark-them-done/requirements.md § R-2
- **artifacts:** requirements.md, scenarios.md

**What each says.** `requirements.md` § R-2 clause 4 uses "a line break" without naming its
characters, and clause 5 demands that the screen accept "exactly the texts the service accepts".
`scenarios.md` uses U+000A alone. Its § Bounds the requirements did not give, item 1, reports that
U+000D, U+0085, U+2028, U+2029, U+000B and U+000C are unstated. It also notes that the guestbook
keeps a next line inside a signature (`text-measurement.json` case `next_line_inside_is_kept`,
present: checked by loading the file).

**Why they cannot both be true.** Clause 5 cannot hold if the two sides each take their own
language's default, and the defaults disagree. Command: `python3 -c` over
`str.splitlines()`, then `node -e` over `/^.*$/`. Output: `python splitlines breaks on: ['LF',
'VT', 'FF', 'CR', 'NEL', 'LS', 'PS']` against `js ... breaks on: [ 'LF', 'CR', 'LS', 'PS' ]`. A
task carrying VT, FF or NEL between two words would be refused by the service and let through by
the screen. That is the `D-04` class of defect `requirements.md` § Edge cases lists as having
happened, and the reason `spec/contexts/guestbook.md` § `BR-01` writes its trim set down ("the
two languages this system is built in disagree about six of them").

**What settles it.** Nothing. Which texts a person may store is a product rule.

**Resolution.** Ask one closed question. (A, recommended) A line break is any of U+000A, U+000B,
U+000C, U+000D, U+0085, U+2028, U+2029: one written set that both sides read and no language
default, so a pasted text is refused identically everywhere. (B) U+000A and U+000D only: the
others stay content, as in a guestbook signature, and the written set is those two. Then add the
chosen set to the new `R-2` clause 6 (COH-requirements-1) and to § Bounds as "| Line break inside
a task | refused; the set is … | `Q-11`, this decision |".

**What was ambiguous.** `requirements.md` § R-2 clause 4 introduced "line break" as a term.
`Q-11`'s wording ("a line break inside a task's text") inherited it, and neither gave the set.

**What was not found.** No artefact asserts which refusal wins when a text is both over 200 and
multi-line. Neither says it, so nothing contradicts. It is not raised here.

## 1. What must become true

`review-converge` knows where its delta entry goes when it runs in the **requirements** stage and edits a file under `spec/` there, such as `spec/invariants.md`. And `add-reconciliation` can record a resolution that is a named assumption awaiting the user, which is neither `auto` nor `hitl`.

## 2. The coupling surface

- A SKILL (`skills/review-converge/SKILL.md`, its delta rule).
- The delta assembly (`skills/_shared/sdd/delta.py`).
- The change record verb `change_state add-reconciliation --source {auto,hitl}`.

## 3. Observed

```text
The review-converge worker's closing block, PROCESS_FAULT (verbatim):
review-converge names a delta directory only for design and spec_sync, yet it is dispatched in
requirements and made to edit spec/invariants.md; delta.py assembles only design/ and reconcile/, so I
put the entry in design/delta/converge.md on my own reading. Separately, add-reconciliation --source
has only auto or hitl, and neither fits a named assumption: it is not a human decision and does not
follow from a higher document. I used auto and spelled that out in --decision.

$ sdd-engine loop back --member review-converge …
OK  COH-requirements-1 -- closed (hitl)
…
OK  COH-requirements-4 -- closed (hitl)          <- resolved by a named assumption (A-1), recorded as REC-… --source auto
OK  COH-requirements-5 -- closed (hitl)
```

**Plugin version:** 0.1.126. Read from the skill base directory (`~/.claude/plugins/cache/scalo/forge/0.1.126/`) and from `sdd-engine loop sent`, which printed `"toolchain": {"chain": "forge 0.1.126"}`.

**Stack:** `fastapi-react-postgres`

**Level:** instance

**Repository, and its commit:** jarekwasowskiscalo/forge-test2-react@68c647394b35c280b17fafeb0f8f4c49cba7fe09

**Its template:** Scalo-Sales-Engineering-Consulting/forge_template_python_react

## 4. Expected, and by which authority

- **Delta.** Constitution Art. IV (as the template carries it): *"Every edit under `spec/` is declared in that change's `delta.md`."* `spec/invariants.md` § Deliberate non-goals says every edit to that file in a change cycle *"belongs to the convergence round"*, which happens in the requirements stage too. The skill names a fragment directory for design and spec_sync only, so a requirements-stage convergence edit under `spec/` has no documented home.
- **Source.** The budget refusal (`loop ask --raise`) prescribes *"a named assumption in this stage's document ("Assumed: ..., say so if not")"*. Art. VIII allows `auto` only when a higher document settles the question, and `hitl` means a person decided. A named assumption is neither, yet the verb forces one of the two. The record then says "closed (hitl)" for a finding no person has decided yet.

## 5. How it was discovered

- **Repository and branch:** jarekwasowskiscalo/forge-test2-react, branch `sdd/CR-2609-823a-todo-list-add-tasks-and-mark-them-done`
- **Change record:** CR-2609-823a ("Todo list - add tasks and mark them done"). No pull request yet.
- **Where in the process:** stage `requirements`. `review-converge` was dispatched by hand after coherence pass 1 (see #306) and edited `requirements.md`, `impact.md` and `spec/invariants.md`.
- **Queue entry:** banked as PROC-9

## 6. Reproduction

1. In the requirements stage, let a coherence finding name `spec/invariants.md` as its ambiguity source (any system-wide non-goal worded for one concept, extended to a second one).
2. Dispatch `review-converge`. It must write a delta entry and finds no requirements-stage directory in its skill.
3. Let another finding be resolved by a named assumption (the budget refusal's exit). `add-reconciliation --source` accepts only `auto|hitl`.

## 7. Root cause, so far

**CONFIRMED (read at the cited lines):**
- The skill's delta rule enumerates design and spec_sync only.
- `delta.py` assembles `design/delta/` and `reconcile/delta/` only.
- The verb's `--source` choice is `{auto,hitl}`.

**Not investigated:** whether `loop close` at the requirements stage assembles `design/delta/` fragments, so that the worker's choice of `design/delta/converge.md` is picked up by `delta-coverage` at that close.

## 8. Why this level cannot fix it alone

The skill, the assembler and the verb are the engine's. An instance cannot add a fragment directory or a `--source` value.

## 9. Proposed resolution

**Proposed:**
- Name the requirements-stage fragment directory in `review-converge`'s delta rule. `design/delta/` is the natural home, since delta.py already assembles it; say so explicitly.
- Add `--source assumed` to `add-reconciliation`, meaning "a named assumption awaiting the stage's human gate", and have the gate's approval turn it into `hitl`. `loop back` would then print "closed (assumed)" rather than "closed (hitl)".

**Rejected, and why:**
- Record assumptions as `auto`, as the worker did. That files a guess under the one source Art. VIII reserves for rulings that follow from a higher document.
- Record them as `hitl`. That claims a person decided before one did.

## 10. Blast radius

- **Which stacks does this touch?** Every stack.
- **Does the other template survive the change unmodified?** Yes.
- **Is it backwards compatible with profiles already committed?** Yes. A new enum value for the verb.
- **Does `schema_version` move?** Possibly, if reconciliation sources are validated by a schema.
- **Does any archived change record stop being readable?** No. `auto` and `hitl` keep their meaning.
- **Which existing tests must change?** The state-verb tests for `add-reconciliation`; the review-converge skill lint for the delta rule.

## 11. Acceptance criteria

1. `skills/review-converge/SKILL.md` names the fragment directory for a requirements-stage round.
2. `sdd-engine change_state add-reconciliation --source assumed …` is accepted. `loop back` reports the finding as closed (assumed). Approving the stage's gate records the human decision.

**Proved by:** new cases in `skills/_shared/sdd/test_sdd_state_verbs.py`, and the skill lint.

## 12. What this repository does meanwhile

- [ ] **Blocked**
- [x] **Working around it** — and the workaround is at: `spec/changes/CR-2609-823a-todo-list-add-tasks-and-mark-them-done/design/delta/converge.md` (the delta entry for `spec/invariants.md`), and the reconciliations for A-1 and A-2 recorded as `auto` with "NOT a human decision" in their `--decision` text.
- [ ] **Nothing** — it was noticed, not hit

**Must the workaround be reverted when this lands?** No. The user's approval of `requirements.md` at the stage gate is the human decision on A-1 and A-2.

## 13. Not this

- Not the dead end that made the hand dispatch necessary (#306).
- Not the write-back of answered questions (#305).

**Its template:** Scalo-Sales-Engineering-Consulting/forge_template_python_react

## 4. Expected, and by which authority

- **Delta.** Constitution Art. IV (as the template carries it): *"Every edit under `spec/` is declared in that change's `delta.md`."* `spec/invariants.md` § Deliberate non-goals says every edit to that file in a change cycle *"belongs to the convergence round"*, which happens in the requirements stage too. The skill names a fragment directory for design and spec_sync only, so a requirements-stage convergence edit under `spec/` has no documented home.
- **Source.** The budget refusal (`loop ask --raise`) prescribes *"a named assumption in this stage's document ("Assumed: ..., say so if not")"*. Art. VIII allows `auto` only when a higher document settles the question, and `hitl` means a person decided. A named assumption is neither, yet the verb forces one of the two. The record then says "closed (hitl)" for a finding no person has decided yet.

## 5. How it was discovered

- **Repository and branch:** jarekwasowskiscalo/forge-test2-react, branch `sdd/CR-2609-823a-todo-list-add-tasks-and-mark-them-done`
- **Change record:** CR-2609-823a ("Todo list - add tasks and mark them done"). No pull request yet.
- **Where in the process:** stage `requirements`. `review-converge` was dispatched by hand after coherence pass 1 (see #306) and edited `requirements.md`, `impact.md` and `spec/invariants.md`.
- **Queue entry:** banked as PROC-9

## 6. Reproduction

1. In the requirements stage, let a coherence finding name `spec/invariants.md` as its ambiguity source (any system-wide non-goal worded for one concept, extended to a second one).
2. Dispatch `review-converge`. It must write a delta entry and finds no requirements-stage directory in its skill.
3. Let another finding be resolved by a named assumption (the budget refusal's exit). `add-reconciliation --source` accepts only `auto|hitl`.

## 7. Root cause, so far

**CONFIRMED (read at the cited lines):**
- The skill's delta rule enumerates design and spec_sync only.
- `delta.py` assembles `design/delta/` and `reconcile/delta/` only.
- The verb's `--source` choice is `{auto,hitl}`.

**Not investigated:** whether `loop close` at the requirements stage assembles `design/delta/` fragments, so that the worker's choice of `design/delta/converge.md` is picked up by `delta-coverage` at that close.

## 8. Why this level cannot fix it alone

The skill, the assembler and the verb are the engine's. An instance cannot add a fragment directory or a `--source` value.

## 9. Proposed resolution

**Proposed:**
- Name the requirements-stage fragment directory in `review-converge`'s delta rule. `design/delta/` is the natural home, since delta.py already assembles it; say so explicitly.
- Add `--source assumed` to `add-reconciliation`, meaning "a named assumption awaiting the stage's human gate", and have the gate's approval turn it into `hitl`. `loop back` would then print "closed (assumed)" rather than "closed (hitl)".

**Rejected, and why:**
- Record assumptions as `auto`, as the worker did. That files a guess under the one source Art. VIII reserves for rulings that follow from a higher document.
- Record them as `hitl`. That claims a person decided before one did.

## 10. Blast radius

- **Which stacks does this touch?** Every stack.
- **Does the other template survive the change unmodified?** Yes.
- **Is it backwards compatible with profiles already committed?** Yes. A new enum value for the verb.
- **Does `schema_version` move?** Possibly, if reconciliation sources are validated by a schema.
- **Does any archived change record stop being readable?** No. `auto` and `hitl` keep their meaning.
- **Which existing tests must change?** The state-verb tests for `add-reconciliation`; the review-converge skill lint for the delta rule.

## 11. Acceptance criteria

1. `skills/review-converge/SKILL.md` names the fragment directory for a requirements-stage round.
2. `sdd-engine change_state add-reconciliation --source assumed …` is accepted. `loop back` reports the finding as closed (assumed). Approving the stage's gate records the human decision.

**Proved by:** new cases in `skills/_shared/sdd/test_sdd_state_verbs.py`, and the skill lint.

- [ ] **Blocked**
- [x] **Working around it** — and the workaround is at: `spec/changes/CR-2609-823a-todo-list-add-tasks-and-mark-them-done/design/delta/converge.md` (the delta entry for `spec/invariants.md`), and the reconciliations for A-1 and A-2 recorded as `auto` with "NOT a human decision" in their `--decision` text.
- [ ] **Nothing** — it was noticed, not hit

**Must the workaround be reverted when this lands?** No. The user's approval of `requirements.md` at the stage gate is the human decision on A-1 and A-2.

## 13. Not this

- Not the write-back of answered questions (#305).

input.content:
## 1. What must become true

A convergence round does not re-dispatch an author to "APPLY" a resolution that `review-converge` has already written into that author's own artefact. For a requirements-stage finding, the earliest ambiguous document *is* the author's artefact, so the round is either skipped for that member or dispatched as what it really is: a check.

## 2. The coupling surface

- The stage composition and the orchestrator's table: row 14e (the convergence loop) and Phase 5.
- The division of labour between `review-converge`, which edits "the earliest ambiguous document", and the round's re-dispatched authors, who "APPLY the recorded resolutions".

## 3. Observed

```text
review-converge (after coherence pass 1) edited, commit a014ab4:
  requirements.md, impact.md, spec/invariants.md, design/delta/converge.md   (REC-1..REC-7)

$ sdd-engine loop next
ACTION  dispatch (row 14e)
           6 finding(s) were resolved since the last round; the documents they named go back to their authors rather than being patched
CONVERGENCE ROUND  1 of 3 -- mode: deep
Send 3 subagent(s) in ONE message.        (cr-impact, cr-requirements, cr-scenarios)

cr-impact's closing block (verbatim, excerpts):
- FILES_WRITTEN: NONE. The one resolution, COH-requirements-6, was already in … impact.md at lines
  381-385, § Tier signals. review-converge added it in commit a014ab4 (+6 lines, the dated
  re-measurement note). The smallest edit that satisfies the resolution was therefore no edit.
- PROCESS_FAULT: A convergence round sent cr-impact to apply COH-requirements-6 after review-converge
  had already written that exact edit into impact.md (a014ab4; the preflight's own EDITED line names
  it), so a full worker dispatch produced a zero-byte diff.

cr-requirements' closing block (verbatim, excerpt):
- EVIDENCE: All six resolutions were already present, because review-converge wrote them in commit
  a014ab4. …
- PROCESS_FAULT: The convergence-round dispatch told cr-requirements to APPLY resolutions that
  review-converge had already written into requirements.md (commit a014ab4). The round was a
  re-verification billed as an application, one full dispatch spent confirming edits already on disk.

Subagent usage for the round: cr-impact 96 116 tokens (zero-byte diff), cr-requirements 124 479 tokens
(four small consistency edits), cr-scenarios 150 573 tokens (the one member whose artefact
review-converge had NOT edited, and the one that had real work).
```

**Plugin version:** 0.1.126. Read from the skill base directory (`~/.claude/plugins/cache/scalo/forge/0.1.126/`) and from `sdd-engine loop sent`, which printed `"toolchain": {"chain": "forge 0.1.126"}`.

**Stack:** `fastapi-react-postgres`

**Level:** instance

**Repository, and its commit:** jarekwasowskiscalo/forge-test2-react@68c647394b35c280b17fafeb0f8f4c49cba7fe09

**Its template:** Scalo-Sales-Engineering-Consulting/forge_template_python_react

## 4. Expected, and by which authority

`skills/sdd/SKILL.md` Phase 5:
- *"`review-converge` … edits the *earliest* ambiguous document, so the next fan-out converges."*
- The convergence round *"re-dispatch[es] the authors the findings' `artifacts` pointed at (told to APPLY the resolutions minimally, never to re-derive)"*, and *"Re-dispatching the author is the point, and it is not interchangeable with patching the artefact."*

Both are coherent when the earliest ambiguous document lies *above* the author's artefact (a design document above a spec, say). In the requirements stage it usually does not: `ambiguity_source` is `requirements.md` or `impact.md` itself. `review-converge` then patches the artefact, and the round sends its author to apply a patch that is already there.

Nothing documents the case where the ambiguity source and the artefact coincide. That is the finding.

## 5. How it was discovered

- **Repository and branch:** jarekwasowskiscalo/forge-test2-react, branch `sdd/CR-2609-823a-todo-list-add-tasks-and-mark-them-done`
- **Change record:** CR-2609-823a ("Todo list - add tasks and mark them done"). No pull request yet.
- **Where in the process:** stage `requirements`, convergence round 1 (deep), after coherence pass 1 and `review-converge`.
- **Queue entry:** banked as PROC-10, seen twice (cr-impact and cr-requirements reported it independently).

## 6. Reproduction

1. A requirements-stage coherence pass files findings whose `ambiguity_source` is `requirements.md` or `impact.md`.
2. `review-converge` resolves them, editing those files, as its skill says.
3. `loop next` → row 14e dispatches `cr-impact` and `cr-requirements` to APPLY the same resolutions. Their diffs are empty or cosmetic.

## 7. Root cause, so far

**CONFIRMED by observation, and by reading Phase 5:**
- The round's member set is "the authors the findings' `artifacts` pointed at", with no subtraction for artefacts `review-converge` already edited (the reconciliation records name them: `--edited`).
- `review-converge` edits the ambiguity source even when it is the artefact itself.

## 8. Why this level cannot fix it alone

The round's composition, row 14e and the two skills' contracts are the engine's. An instance cannot change which members `loop next` renders.

## 9. Proposed resolution

**Proposed:** when computing a deep round's members, drop any author whose every named artefact appears in the pass's reconciliation records as `--edited` by `review-converge`. Leave the coherence verify round to check those edits. Alternatively, in stages where the ambiguity source is the artefact, have `review-converge` record the decision only, and leave the edit to the author's round, so exactly one of the two writes it.

**Rejected, and why:** keep both and tell the author to "verify" instead of "apply". That still spends a full dispatch per author to read what the next coherence pass reads anyway.

## 10. Blast radius

- **Which stacks does this touch?** Every stack.
- **Does the other template survive the change unmodified?** Yes.
- **Is it backwards compatible with profiles already committed?** Yes.
- **Does `schema_version` move?** No.
- **Does any archived change record stop being readable?** No.
- **Which existing tests must change?** The `loop next` round-composition tests.

## 11. Acceptance criteria

1. A fixture pass whose two findings both name `requirements.md` as ambiguity source and artefact: after `review-converge` records reconciliations editing `requirements.md`, `loop next`'s deep round does not include `cr-requirements`, and goes straight to the verify round when no other author is owed.

**Proved by:** a new test beside the `loop next` round-composition tests.

## 12. What this repository does meanwhile

- [ ] **Blocked**
- [ ] **Working around it** — and the workaround is at: <!-- path -->
- [x] **Nothing** — it was noticed, not hit. The round ran as rendered, and cr-impact banked a nil return with its reason.

**Must the workaround be reverted when this lands?** There is none.

## 13. Not this

- Not a change to what `review-converge` may edit.
- Not the hand dispatch of `review-converge` in this change (#306). The duplication would occur in the rendered flow too.

# Escalation to the fable tier

What `SKILL.md` § B. Interrupts (rows 7c and 7d) and the offer rows (14e1, 27a1, 39a, 51a) rest
on. The paragraph a fable dispatch carries stays in `SKILL.md` under `<escalation_paragraph>`,
because it is inserted verbatim; this is the reasoning around it.

**Fable is never automatic.** The only paths to the fable tier read the record: the manual
one is `sdd-engine dispatch escalation-check --cr {cr_id}` (row 7d), and the computed one is
`escalation.apply_overrides`, which flips a member only when an answered `ESC-*` question
names that skill and is not yet consumed. Without such an answer both refuse. The recorded
question, with the cost in its text, is the audit trail of who spent that money — and it is
the *condition* of spending it rather than the convention around it. `MODEL_ROUTING`
deliberately contains no fable entry, `model_for` never returns one, and fitness tests keep
both true.

**The OFFER is automatic; the SPEND never is.** At three measured failure thresholds —
a convergence round ≥ 2 (rows 14e1/27a1), the first `build-debug` of a debug entry
(row 39a), and the re-review after a turn-back (row 51a) — the preflight replaces the
dispatch with a READY escalation question: the code drafts the text with the price from
`.specconf/pricing.json`, `sdd-engine loop ask` records and asks it, the human answers once. A
declined instance never re-asks (the qid is the memory); a bought one covers exactly the
named dispatches and `sdd-engine loop sent` consumes it — one attempt on fable, then back to opus
unless a new instance offers again. These three offers recommend the DECLINE, because
cheaper rungs remain; row 7c keeps recommending the purchase, because there everything
cheaper has already failed.

## The flag, and the defect before it

Before the flag existed this row was broken and looked fine: it resets the ladder *before*
re-dispatching, so the rung went back to `not_started` and the model resolved to the base
tier. The table promised fable, the prompt said opus, and only a human comparing the two
would ever have noticed.

{
        "Model rates in USD per million tokens. DATA, not code -- and that is this file's",
        "whole argument. One price table in this repository lived with the vendor",
        "(the vendored claude-history server, _PRICING) and went stale on April",
        "2026: every new model fell through to Sonnet's default rate, so an Opus 5 session",
        "read three times cheaper than it was. A price table goes stale -- so let it go stale",
        "in a data file that has a date rather than in code that does not.",
        "",
        "THE KEY IS MODEL x SPEED. `message.usage.speed` really does stand in a session's",
        "record (measured on CR-2608-f9b6: `standard` on 5 367 turns, `fast` on 0, the field",
        "absent on 2 996 -- sessions from Claude Code 2.1.234). Fast mode is therefore a",
        "measurable item rather than a hypothesis, and gets its own `<model>:fast` entry.",
        "",
        "THE FAST RATES ARE WRITTEN DOWN, NOT COMPUTED. Fast mode is $10 input and $50",
        "output per MTok, available for Opus 5 and Opus 4.8 alone. The cache multipliers stack",
        "ON THE FAST PRICE, so a 5 min write = 1.25 x 10 = 12.50, an hourly write = 2 x 10 =",
        "20, and a hit = 0.1 x 10 = 1.00. Those three numbers stand here as numbers: this file",
        "is a price list rather than a calculator, and a reader is not to recreate the",
        "multipliers from memory.",
        "",
        "FABLE 5.1 READS ITS CACHE AT 0.025 x, NOT 0.1 x. $0.25 per MTok against a $10 input",
        "is a quarter of Fable 5's $1.00 and looks like a misplaced decimal; it is the rate.",
        "Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 are the only models with that multiplier -- every",
        "other entry here is the standard 0.1 x -- so the two lines below are the reason a reader",
        "must not derive a cache rate from the input rate, on this table or any other.",
        "",
        "A MISSING `:fast` ENTRY IS INFORMATION, NOT AN OVERSIGHT. Opus 4.7 errors on",
        "`speed: \"fast\"`, and Opus 4.6 runs standard and is priced that way. That is why",
        "`pricing.rate()` must not fall through to the standard rate when somebody asks about",
        "`claude-opus-4-7:fast` -- a missing rate is an answer.",
        "",
        "What is NOT here and why: the 1.1 x multiplier for `inference_geo: \"us\"`, because a",
        "session's record carries no geography at all, and a rate applied on a guess lies",
        "exactly as much as a stale one. `batch_discount` is here, but it applies only where",
        "`service_tier` in the record says `batch`.",
        "",
        "Updating: raise `as_of`, correct the numbers, leave the entries of retired models --",
        "the session corpus is older than the current line-up and has a right to be priced."
    ],
    "schema_version": 1,

The preflight's own header: *"spelled out, do not go looking for the flags"*. A worker is told to trust this line over `--help`, so the line must be exact. In argparse's own usage grammar, `X ...` means repeated values of one flag, and the verb's help says "repeat per edited document".

content.text:
Here is the approval of the requirements. It's the last step of this stage, and the cheapest moment to say "that's not what I meant".

**Open and read:** `spec/changes/CR-2609-823a-todo-list-add-tasks-and-mark-them-done/requirements.md` (the scenarios and impact document are in the same folder).

**The 11 requirements, in short**
- **R-1 Adding a task:** you type in the field and add; the task appears at the top.
- **R-2 What isn't a task is refused,** each with a clear reason: empty or only spaces, over 200 characters, or a line break inside. The screen refuses exactly what the app refuses.
- **R-3 One shared list:** everybody sees the same list, newest first, and an empty list says so.
- **R-4 Done and not done:** ticking marks a task done (it stays in its place, shown as done), and ticking again undoes it. Two people ticking at once don't cancel each other out.
- **R-5 Two screens:** navigation between the guestbook and the to-do list; the main address still opens the guestbook.
- **R-6 Editing:** same rules as adding; editing never changes done or not done.
- **R-7 Deleting:** asks "are you sure?" first, then the task is gone for good.
- **R-8 A task someone else already deleted:** editing, ticking or deleting it gives a clear message, and it never comes back.
- **R-9 Two people changing one task:** the later change wins, but an edit never undoes a tick, or the other way round.
- **R-10 A change that failed** (for example, the app can't be reached) is never shown as made.
- **R-11 Example tasks** in a new test environment: at least three, one of them done; each list is filled on its own; never in production; never duplicated. A person checks this one.

**Four assumptions that your approval turns into decisions.** They exist because the process ran out of questions for this stage:
- **A-1:** "Line break" means any of the **7** invisible line-break characters, from one list both halves of the app read. *Alternative:* only the 2 common ones.
- **A-2:** A task stays **until somebody deletes it**. Nothing removes old tasks automatically.
- **A-3:** The line-break check looks at the text **after spaces are trimmed from the ends**, so an invisible character can't smuggle a line break in.
- **A-4:** The existing guestbook tests stay as they are. The one exception: the screen test may follow a renamed header or link, if you approve a new name in the mock-up later.
